clue.text: Strand is found in empty workshop

indicators.note: to be found inside something is to sit within it, so one piece goes inside another
an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A loose thread turns up lying in a workshop that has been cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like the verb of the sentence but is itself the inserted piece: W(IS)P.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisp is a thin, fine piece of something such as hair or straw, much like a single strand.

clue.text: Taste fish, eating last of coley

indicators.note: something that eats takes food inside itself, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: a trout is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone samples a fish dish while eating the end of a piece of coley.
explanation.walkthrough: Coley is another fish, which keeps the surface in the kitchen; only its last letter matters. TR(Y)OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To try out a thing is to test or sample it, as one would taste a new dish before deciding.

clue.text: Blonde head, just quality?

parts.note: fair hair is light-coloured, blonde
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: It reads like a question about whether having fair hair is merely a superficial trait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests a head of hair after 'Blonde', but it is the geographical sense, a headland, found in place names such as Loch Ness and Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairness is the quality of being just, treating everyone impartially and even-handedly.

clue.text: Standard that may be fixed in centrefold?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a basic, regular item

definitions.text: that may be fixed in centrefold
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the small wire clip fixed through the middle fold of a magazine

explanation.surface: It suggests a standard feature that might be pinned up as a magazine's centrefold picture.
explanation.walkthrough: A centrefold is the middle spread of a magazine, which is exactly where the binding wire clips go.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a main or regular product, and also the bent metal fastener binding pages together.

clue.text: Ahead by four or nine, perhaps, prepare for fight

parts.note: four and nine are square numbers, two times two and three times three
a team that is ahead is up, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: A team leading by four or nine points readies itself for a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead by four or nine' reads as a scoreline, but 'by' simply places the two pieces side by side, and the numbers are examples of a kind of number.
explanation.definitionFit: To square up is to adopt a fighting stance and face an opponent, getting ready to throw punches.

clue.text: Stretch to grab bar, having missed a ring

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so one piece closes around another

parts.note: a stretch is a period of time, as in a stretch in prison

indicators.note: what is missed is left out, so a letter drops away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A gymnast stretches for a bar but misses the rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' reads as a gymnast's hoop, but it is a noun for the sound of a voice or instrument; 'a' is the letter dropped, not an article.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the characteristic tone or resonance of a voice or instrument, its distinctive ring.

clue.text: Some paper in off-white, guillotined

indicators.note: a guillotine beheads its victim, so the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: cream is a yellowish off-white colour

explanation.surface: Sheets of off-white paper are cut to size on a paper guillotine.
explanation.walkthrough: A guillotine is also the office tool for trimming paper, which hides the beheading instruction; CREAM loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a fixed quantity of paper sheets, traditionally 480 and now usually 500.

clue.text: Key left to be collected by fellow: it is outside

indicators.note: whatever is collected is gathered up and held, so it sits inside its collector

parts.note: taken as written; it wraps everything else

indicators.note: something outside wraps around all the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: a fellow is a man
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A spare key has been left for a man to pick up; it is waiting outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest, one inside the other. Port is the nautical word for the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Key used as an adjective means crucial or of central significance, as in a key witness.

clue.text: Necessary nutrient for figure injected with iodine

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so one piece receives another

parts.note: ten is a number, a figure
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A dietary supplement is described as vital for a good figure and administered with iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'figure' look like 'nutrient for your figure', but each is a piece: PRO + TE(I)N.
explanation.definitionFit: Protein is one of the essential components of diet, required for building and repairing body tissue.

clue.text: Pretty pack in back of store

parts.note: to pack something in is to give it up, to quit

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something attractive is being packaged in the stockroom at the rear of a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adjective meaning attractive, but it is the adverb, as in pretty good. 'pack in' is a British idiom for give up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty and quite are both adverbs meaning fairly or to a moderate degree, as in pretty warm.

clue.text: Still collection kept here?

parts.note: surface reading: a place where a collection is still being kept, perhaps a museum
setter's reading: a still is a single photographic image, so this is where such stills are collected

explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb meaning yet, but it is a noun: a still is a frozen image from film or a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of mounted pictures holds a collection of snapshots, the still images a camera takes.

clue.text: I told you about a time in scene of action

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is wrapped round another

parts.note: 'There!' is what you say when you have been proved right: there, I told you so
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone says I told you so about something that happened at the scene of the incident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There!' is the triumphant exclamation of someone proved right, so 'I told you' stands for that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre of war is the region where fighting takes place, hence a scene of military operations.

clue.text: Narrow recorder, might you say?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to become gradually thinner towards one end
second meaning, a whimsical coinage: one who tapes things

explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' suggests the musical instrument; the question mark and 'might you say' flag an invented word for someone who records on tape.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means become thinner towards a point; read as tape plus -er it means a person making tape recordings.

clue.text: Leader dropped from most difficult peak

indicators.note: the leader is the opening letter, and dropping it removes it

parts.note: severest means hardest, most difficult

explanation.surface: An expedition leader is forced off the hardest mountain to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVEREST loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Everest in the Himalayas is the highest mountain summit on Earth, an example of a peak.

clue.text: Wise Men, for example, travelling there

indicators.note: letters that are travelling are on the move, shifting into new positions

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Magi journey to Bethlehem in the nativity story.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the number of Wise Men, not who they were.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradition counts the Magi as a trio, so the Wise Men exemplify that number of people.

clue.text: Pointless draughtsman using it?

parts.note: surface reading: a futile designer resorting to some tool
setter's reading: the draughtsman's drawing implement has lost its point and needs restoring

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' means futile on the surface, but literally it is a blunt drawing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughtsman with a blunt lead would use a small bladed device to restore the tip of the drawing instrument.

clue.text: Angriest when provoked, one doesn't usually react

indicators.note: provoked means stirred up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A placid person who rarely responds, yet is at their angriest when provoked.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a reading about temperament; the definition is chemistry, where reacting means forming compounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble gases such as argon and neon are called inert because they seldom combine chemically with other elements.

clue.text: A weapon found in heather, scary

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something found in another lies within it, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: ling is another name for common heather
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: Discovering a gun hidden among the heather on a moor would be frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: Ling is the plant name for heather, also a fish: A + L(ARM)ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alarming causes fear or worry, the same sense as frightening or scary.

clue.text: Egg on jokers, idiots

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece stacks over the second

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
wits are clever, funny people, jokers

explanation.surface: Someone eggs on a bunch of pranksters, the fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' looks like the phrase meaning urge, but 'Egg' is a noun and 'on' just places it above.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitwits is an informal insult for foolish or stupid people, a synonym of idiots.

clue.text: Titian first for Van Gogh, say?

parts.note: titian is a reddish-brown colour, named after the painter's hair tones
the head is the first or front part, as in head of the queue

explanation.surface: It sounds like art history: Titian ranked ahead of Van Gogh.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian and Van Gogh are both painters, but Titian here is the hair colour. Van Gogh had red hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A redhead is a person with ginger hair, and Van Gogh's self-portraits show his red beard and hair.

clue.text: Motorist's club?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who drives a car
second meaning: the golf club used for long tee shots

explanation.walkthrough: 'Motorist's club' suggests a motoring association such as the AA; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The same noun names a person at the wheel of a vehicle and the largest-headed golf wood.

clue.text: Leave high and dry in arid place

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a barren, waterless region

explanation.surface: Someone is stranded and abandoned in a barren wasteland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high and dry' chimes with 'arid', making one scene from two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means abandon or forsake; as a noun, a barren waterless region such as the Sahara.

clue.text: Bitter about assignment, John for example

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: bitter is a type of British beer, an ale
a post is a job or appointment one is assigned to

explanation.surface: A man called John resents the task he has been given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like an adjective for John's mood, but it is the pub drink, a hoppy British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: John was one of the twelve disciples whom Jesus chose, so he exemplifies that group.

clue.text: Genesis in print schedule

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
to set a time is to schedule it

explanation.surface: The Book of Genesis appears in a printed timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis suggests the Bible book or the band, but here it is a common noun for a start.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means origin or beginning, and the outset is the start of something.

clue.text: Adult presumably getting this right: my tone wrong

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of place and must be reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grown-up thinks they have it right, but their tone comes out all wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' and 'wrong' sit side by side, yet 'right' is fodder and 'wrong' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person aged between thirty and thirty-nine is surely a grown-up, hence the hedging presumably.

clue.text: Set up separate trick

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, turning the word round

parts.note: to part is to separate

explanation.surface: Someone arranges an elaborate ruse to split people up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' doubles as the phrase for a framing, but here it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a ruse to catch someone out, and a trick can mean exactly such a snare.

clue.text: Gazing at pink elephants primarily, stare in wonder

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only opening letters are taken

parts.note: the initial letter of each word

explanation.surface: A drunk is seeing pink elephants and staring at them in amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: Seeing pink elephants is a jokey way of describing drunken hallucinations.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stare open-mouthed, typically in astonishment or wonder.

clue.text: Piece of earthenware, natural sphere

indicators.note: a piece is a fragment, so a run of letters is taken from the text

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A shard of earthenware pottery has a naturally round shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sphere' suggests a ball, but it is the abstract sense, a field of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean a field of activity or interest, as in the political arena or sphere.

clue.text: Knights trapped by wicked pursuer? They aren't the first!

indicators.note: whatever is trapped is shut inside, held within something else
wicked suggests something twisted or perverse, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the chess notation for a knight, so two knights are NN

explanation.surface: Two knights are caught by an evil chaser, and they come in behind the leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idea that a pursuer, by definition, is never in front; the exclamation mark flags the playful wording.
explanation.definitionFit: Runners-up are competitors finishing behind the winner, so they did not take first place.
